name: ping
why: Supplied adapter answers ping with status ready.

name: spec_dsu_example
why: Example from the specification: 0-1 -> [3,2]; 1-2 -> [2,3]; 0-2 repeated -> [2,3]; self-union 3-3 -> [2,3].

name: spec_kruskal_example
why: Example from the specification: take w=2 (id1) and w=3 (id2), skip w=4 (cycle); vertex 3 isolated -> 2 components, cost 5.

name: spec_prim_example
why: Same graph as spec_kruskal_example: Prim must agree on cost 5 and 2 components.

name: spec_scc_example
why: Example from the specification: 0<->1 form one SCC, 2 and 3 are singletons; cross pairs {0,1}->2 (two input edges, one pair) and 2->3.

name: spec_topo_example
why: Example from the specification: 0 and 1 before 2, 2 before 3.

name: spec_dag_example
why: Example from the specification: d1=3 (id0), d2=min(8, 3-7)=-4 (id2), d3=-4+4=0 (id3), vertex 4 unreachable.

name: kruskal_total_beyond_32bit
why: Three edges of weight 1e9 on a path: cost 3e9 > 2^31-1, needs 64-bit totals.

name: dsu_repeated_unions
why: The same union repeated three times merges once: [2,2] each time.

name: dsu_empty
why: n=0 and no operations: no states are produced.

name: dsu_self_union
why: union(1,1) changes nothing: 3 components, largest 1.

name: kruskal_empty
why: Empty graph is valid: zero cost, no edges, zero components.

name: kruskal_isolates
why: One edge 0-1 (w=5); vertices 2 and 3 are isolates, so 3 components.

name: kruskal_loop_parallel_negative
why: Loop id0 is ignored even though it is the cheapest. Parallel 0-1 edges: take id2 (w=3) over id1 (w=7). Then 1-2 id3 (w=-2). Cost 3-2 = 1.

name: kruskal_ties
why: Triangle with equal weights: any 2 edges are optimal, cost 2.

name: prim_forest_restart
why: Component {0,1,2}: edges w=1 (id1) and w=2 (id2), cost 3. Component {3,4}: id3 w=-5. Vertex 5 isolate. Total -2, 3 components; Prim must restart twice.

name: prim_loop_parallel_negative
why: Same graph as kruskal_loop_parallel_negative: Prim must give the same cost 1.

name: prim_empty
why: Empty graph.

name: scc_basic
why: 0->1->2->0 is a cycle, so {0,1,2} is one SCC; 3 and 4 are singletons. Condensation: C(0..2)->C(3) via 2->3 and C(3)->C(4) via 3->4.

name: scc_loop_parallel
why: A self-loop does not merge anything; parallel 0->1 edges produce one condensation pair only.

name: scc_empty
why: Empty graph.

name: topo_diamond
why: 0->1,0->2,1->3,2->3: 0 must be first and 3 last; [0,2,1,3] and [0,1,2,3] are both valid.

name: topo_cycle
why: 1->2->1 is a directed cycle: false and empty order.

name: topo_self_loop
why: A self-loop 1->1 is a directed cycle of length 1.

name: topo_isolates
why: No edges: every permutation is valid.

name: topo_empty
why: Empty graph is acyclic with an empty order.

name: dag_basic
why: d(1)=2 via id0. d(2)=min(6, 2+3)=5 via id2. d(3)=min(5-1, 2+10)=4 via id3 (negative weight). Vertex 4 has no incoming edge: null / -1.

name: dag_cycle_unreachable
why: 2<->3 is a cycle that source 0 cannot reach; the whole graph is checked, so the answer is false with two empty arrays.

name: dag_ties_parallel
why: Parallel 0->1 edges id0 and id1 both weigh 5; d(2)=6 both via id3 directly and via 1 (5+1). Several witnesses are valid.

name: dag_single_vertex
why: Minimum n=1: source distance 0, parent -1.

name: dag_source_in_middle
why: Source 1: vertex 0 only points INTO the source, so it is unreachable; d(2)=-3.
